carpet.rule.optimizedEntityCollection.de: Uses a section-local spatial index to optimize Lithium push candidate collection. Entity iteration order may change.
carpet.rule.optimizedClimbableTagCheck.d: Caches the CLIMBABLE block-tag lookup used by Lithium entity pushability checks, reducing repeated tag lookups in LivingEntity.onClimbable. The cache is invalidated after data-pack reloads.
carpet.rule.betterNoAiNbt.desc: Skips AI logic (Mob.serverAiStep) for entities carrying the NoBrainAI NBT tag, while keeping passive motion such as gravity, fluids, entity pushing, crush damage, explosion knockback, pistons and riding. Unlike vanilla NoAI, the entity does not freeze in mid-air.
carpet.rule.betterNoAiNbt.extra.0: /data merge entity <target> {NoBrainAI:1b} to set, {NoBrainAI:0b} or /data remove entity <target> NoBrainAI to clear; the tag is saved with the entity and can also be written in /summon NBT
carpet.rule.betterNoAiNbt.extra.1: Skipped: target selector, goal selector, navigation, sensing, brain, and movement/look/jump controls
carpet.rule.betterNoAiNbt.extra.2: Kept: gravity and ground friction, water and bubble columns, entity pushing and crush damage, explosion knockback, pistons, riding (a player can still steer the mount), burning, item pickup, distance-based despawn
carpet.rule.betterNoAiNbt.extra.3: Note: the AI-independent noActionTime no longer accumulates, so the entity will not despawn from 600 ticks of inactivity near a player (same as vanilla NoAI); bosses such as the Ender Dragon or Wither stop their phase progression while tagged
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayChance.desc: Chance for a whitelisted mob to have its AI temporarily disabled. The roll happens once, the first time the entity is about to run AI; only when the random value is below this chance is the AI suppressed. Passive motion (gravity, fluids, entity pushing, crush damage, explosion knockback, pistons, riding) is kept.
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayChance.extra.0: 0 (default) disables the feature entirely; an empty entity list also disables it. Suggested values: 0 and 0.1 (the rule does not restrict the value, anything between 0 and 1 works)
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayChance.extra.1: The roll result is stored in the entity's MobAi NBT field, so reloading a chunk never re-rolls it; every entity is decided exactly once
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayWhitelist.desc: Comma-separated whitelist of mobs eligible for AI delays. Entries are entity ids (minecraft:pig) or entity type tags (#zombies); prefix an entry with ! to exclude it. A list with only exclusions means 'everything except those'; an empty list disables the feature.
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayWhitelist.extra.0: Example: minecraft:pig,#zombies,!#undead - pigs and zombie-like mobs, but never undead ones. Suggested values: !minecraft:drowned (default, every mob except drowned) and !minecraft:drowned,!minecraft:piglin
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayWhitelist.extra.1: Matching: union of all positive entries, minus every negative entry; hitting any positive entry is enough
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayWhitelist.extra.2: Tags are data-pack tags matched by name; a tag that is not loaded behaves as an empty set (matches nothing)
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayTicks.desc: How many ticks a suppressed entity stays without AI before its AI is restored; must be a positive number.
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayTicks.extra.0: Counted in ticks experienced by the entity and saved with it (the remaining time is exactly the MobAi NBT field)
carpet.rule.mobAIDelayTicks.extra.1: A negative remaining time means 'decided: AI is not suppressed' - that is also the state after the AI has been restored
carpet.rule.commandSpawnWhitedListedPlay: Used to summon fake players without prefix
/player <name> spawn original - summon a fake player without prefix
carpet.rule.commandExceedChunkMarker.des: Controls the permission level of ECM command. Invalid when ECM is not started.
carpet.rule.commandExceedChunkMarker.ext: /exceedChunkMarker <dimension> - Show information of the selected dimension
/exceedChunkMarker [dimension] setTopY <topY> - Set the ECM height of the selected dimension (dimension defaults to the player's current dimension)
/exceedChunkMarker [dimension] clear - Clear ECM data of the selected dimension (dimension defaults to the player's current dimension)
/exceedChunkMarker [dimension] loadFromWorld - Load ECM data from world data of the selected dimension (dimension defaults to the player's current dimension)
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.desc: Command to view and control entity IDs
carpet.rule.commandLoadedChunkFinder.des: Records connected chunks that are active during a certain period, used to find forgotten chunk loaders.
carpet.rule.commandLoadedChunkFinder.ext: /loadedChunkFinder - Record chunk loading in the current dimension within 1 tick
/loadedChunkFinder <dimension> [tick] - Record chunk loading in the specified dimension for a specified duration, tick defaults to 1
carpet.rule.commandPacketLoggerPlus.desc: Records the pre-compression size of various packets.
carpet.rule.commandPacketLoggerPlus.extr: /packetLogger stop - Stop recording and display data
carpet.rule.commandRequirementModify.des: Modify permission requirements of specified commands
carpet.rule.commandRequirementModify.ext: /requirementModify <commandPath> <permission> set - Set the permission requirement of the specified command to the given permission
/requirementModify <commandPath> <permission> add - Add a permission requirement on top of the existing requirements
/requirementModify <commandPath> <permission> or - Add an OR-condition permission requirement on top of the existing requirements
/requirementModify <commandPath> clear - Clear permission modifications for the specified command
/requirementModify clearAll - Clear permission modifications for all commands
/requirementModify list - List all commands with modified permission requirements
For commandPath, use <> to indicate parameters:
means setting the permission requirement of "player <player> shadow" to ops
carpet.rule.commandRulesSearcher.desc: Adds a subcommand 'search' to carpet, allowing to search carpet rules by keyword
carpet.rule.commandRulesSearcher.extra.0: /carpet search <key> [isNoDefaultValue] [category] - Search carpet rules, key is the search keyword, isNoDefaultValue whether to search only rules with changed default value (default false), category is the rule category
carpet.rule.commandTickSprintFull.desc: Adds a 'full' argument to /tick sprint that prints the duration of every game tick while sprinting
/tick sprint <time> full - Sprint for the given time and print each tick's duration
Prints a duration summary (average/p50/p95/p99/max/tps) when the sprint ends
carpet.rule.enderPearlForcedTickMinSpeed: Applies new loading logic to ender pearls with speed above a certain threshold, which is more stable and requires fewer loaded chunks.
The set value indicates the self-loading speed threshold. Set to a negative value to disable.
For pearls with the new loading logic, the loading behavior differs significantly from vanilla.
carpet.rule.exceedChunkMarker.desc: Prerequisite for raycast optimization, may cause additional storage (generally only increases save size by less than 0.1%)
carpet.rule.exceedChunkMarker.extra.0: When enabling for the first time, be sure to load once with /exceedChunkMarker
carpet.rule.optimizeRaycast.desc: Optimizes raycast via ECM. Ensure ECM is enabled and has been loaded from the save before turning on.
carpet.rule.optimizeRaycast.extra.0: Known feature: Projectiles will ignore entity hitboxes at some specific positions.
carpet.rule.optimizeForcedEnderPearlTick: Only available when better pearl self-loading is enabled. In most cases, prevents high-speed pearls from generating new chunks, greatly reducing save size. When ECM is not enabled, only pearls outside world height will not generate chunks.
Known feature: Pearls will ignore entity hitboxes that are not loaded.
true - Enable optimization, and pearl behavior matches current version
1_21_2- - Enable optimization, and pearl behavior matches version 1.21.2 and below
1_21_2+ - Enable optimization, and pearl behavior matches version 1.21.2 and above
carpet.rule.optimizedExplosion.desc: Once this many explosions hit the same point within one game tick, the block calculation is skipped when a worst-case check proves no block can be destroyed; only entities are affected
carpet.rule.optimizedExplosion.extra.1: Only same-tick explosions with identical coordinates and power
carpet.rule.mergeTNTNext.desc: A more aggressive TNT merging scheme, may cause unexpected results. Cannot be used together with other TNT merging rules.
carpet.rule.mergeTNTOnlyNether.desc: Specialized TNT merging function. For some specific machines.
carpet.rule.tntPacketOptimization.desc: Optimizes TNT entities by removing unnecessary TNT entity packets (Fuse) and reducing packet frequency
When too many entities of the same type are spawned in the same tick, reduces the packet sending distance for excess entities. Used for optimization of large-yield pearl cannons.
Set to a negative number to disable
carpet.rule.entitySpawnPacketLimitTicksT: Sets the packet sending distance for entities that are limited
carpet.rule.entitySpawnPacketLimitSecond: When too many entities of the same type are spawned in the same second, probabilistically prevents tracking and packet sending of that entity type.
Set to a negative number to disable
carpet.rule.particlesPacketsRange.desc: This distance only affects forced particle packets. But most particles are forced.
carpet.rule.piglinLootItemDelay.desc: Only items that have been present for a certain time will be picked up by piglins
For piglins stacked to a certain amount, suppress AI of some of them.
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.extra.0: /entityID - Show the next 5 entity IDs to be generated
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.extra.1: /entityID show <count> - Show the specified number of entity IDs to be generated
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.extra.2: /entityID show <beginID> <endID> - Show entity IDs within the specified range
carpet.rule.commandEntityIDSet.extra.0: /entityID set <id> - Set the current entity ID to the specified value
carpet.rule.optimizedFakePlayerTick.desc: Trims client sync/advancement/stats/Waypoint per-tick logic for Carpet fake players, keeping main-hand item tick and behavior simulation
carpet.rule.optimizedFakePlayerTick.extr: May affect fake player stats, advancements, scoreboard auto-sync and locator bar display
carpet.rule.randomTickChunkCache.desc: Reuses the random-tick chunk list, refreshed every 40 gt; when disabled, vanilla iteration is used
carpet.rule.spawningChunkCache.desc: Reuses the natural-spawning candidate chunk list, refreshed every 40 gt; when disabled, vanilla iteration is used
carpet.rule.asyncRandomTick.desc: Precomputes the next tick's random-tick candidates off-thread; falls back to vanilla when the result is invalid
carpet.rule.asyncNaturalSpawning.desc: Precomputes natural-spawning candidates off-thread; entity creation and counting stay on the main thread
carpet.rule.asyncNaturalSpawning.extra.0: Falls back to vanilla when data is unavailable or stale
carpet.rule.enderPearlForcedSync.desc: Keeps a pearl's tick in sync with the world tick despite async chunk loading delays
carpet.rule.entitySpawnPacketLimitSecond: Throttled entities regain vanilla tracking distance after surviving this many ticks
Set to a negative value to disable
No effect on the per-tick limit
carpet.rule.optimizeItemMerge.desc: Fills item stacks to a full stack to reduce lag (minor effect)
carpet.rule.optimizeItemMerge.extra.0: Partial merging: drops fill up to a full stack first, the remainder stays in the original drop
carpet.rule.mergeTNTNext.extra.1: TRUE: old explosion handling; moving merged TNT behaves unlike vanilla
carpet.rule.mergeTNTNext.extra.2: SAFE: safer explosion handling; moving merged TNT behaves like vanilla
carpet.rule.mergeTNTNext.extra.3: AlmostVanilla: merges only when TNT explodes, keeping TNT tick order
carpet.rule.mergeTNTNext.extra.4: AlmostVanilla should not change TNT behaviour; report any vanilla mismatch as an issue
carpet.rule.mergeTNTNextExplosion.desc: Merges the multiple explosions produced by one merged TNT into a single explosion, so entities are affected only once. Only applies when TNT merging is enabled and the explosion is proven unable to destroy any block.
Requires mergeTNTNext to be a mode other than False
Only explosions that cannot destroy any block are merged
Damage and knockback are applied once instead of once per merged TNT
Forced particle packets use a fixed distance of 512, unaffected by this rule
